title: The Platonic Realm
description: If mathematical objects exist somewhere, they exist here. Unlocks the Platonic Compass.

puzzle.goal: At every vertex of a convex polyhedron the face angles θ_j fall short of a full turn; that shortfall is the vertex's angular deficit. Sum the deficits over all V vertices: the total depends only on the shape's topology, through the number V − E + F.
puzzle.name: Descartes' theorem on total angular defect (discrete Gauss–Bonnet)
puzzle.form: sum ( n , 1 , V , 2 * π - sumk ( j , θ _ j ) )
puzzle.ask: For a convex solid χ = 2, so the deficits total 4π. In a regular solid each vertex joins q regular p-gons (angle (p−2)π/p each). Find the number of vertices V of the dodecahedron (pentagons, three at each vertex).
puzzle.method: Flatten the corners: each vertex's deficit is 2π minus its face angles. Count all face angles face by face (each p-gon has angle sum (p−2)π) and use V − E + F.
